name: Brussels Sprouts (High Raffinose & Sulfur Gas Warning)
whyItWorks: Brussels sprouts contain high concentrations of raffinose (an indigestible trisaccharide) and glucosinolates. Colonic fermentation generates extreme volumes of carbon dioxide and hydrogen sulfide gas, causing agonizing abdominal distension.
prepOrOrderInstructions: Flare Warning: Avoid Brussels sprouts during active IBD. Even in remission, eat only 2–3 well-cooked halved sprouts at a time.
watchOuts: Severe gas pressure against inflamed intestinal walls can trigger severe flares and spasm episodes.
